metadata.note: Utility teardown of runtime/scripts/build_cli_d3_reels.py — the 432-line batch orchestrator that turns a folder of already-built D3 sim HTMLs into Claude-skin CLI-explainer review cuts, one reel per sim, unattended. For each sim in a JSON config it (1) stamps the reel's beat_sheet.json using a fixed 10-beat template with the ClaudeComposerAsk cold open, ClaudeCodeBeat CODE beat carrying the sim's OWN inline JS, and ClaudeTitleOutro; (2) shells out to capture_sim.py for baseline + change mp4s; (3) generates Kokoro audio at am_onyx with the --no-gate flag; (4) renders the Claude-skin Remotion beats (soft-fail — un-rendered beats compile as slates); (5) runs compile.py --review then compile.py master; (6) appends a pipe-delimited row to CLI-EXPLAINERS-OVERNIGHT-LOG.md. Idempotence: if <slug>-slate.mp4 already exists AND is >50KB the sim is skipped. The three laws stamped into every sim's beat sheet: COLD OPEN LAW (B00 ClaudeComposerAsk carries its own RESULT lines), ACTUAL-CODE LAW (B03 ClaudeCodeBeat quotes the sim's actual inline JS, trimmed by extract_code() from the longest inline <script> block, never pseudocode), HANDOFF LAW (B08 ClaudeComposerAsk with the viewer's Your-Turn prompt typed in). The tool wraps sims, it does not invent them — the D3 sim was already generated by Claude in a prior step. Playlist adaptation for @HumanitariansAI: composer folder chip reads @HumanitariansAI; outro card is the locked ClaudeTitleOutro with hardcoded @NikBearBrown handle per OUTRO-LOCK.md — flagged in README.md for the human reviewer before publication. episode.source_sha256 6d2d56ae2262b93e8d5864933bcd5c9dbd3c3b79a39a222b5a03b3a98356722f (from invocation); current file sha 256 c37d17288291b4b7ca3ec7e06a23863f99b5c1c29c9f80554330829f459d172d.

beats.role_note: MECHANISM 3 — extract_code() enforces ACTUAL-CODE LAW. Regex over inline <script> tags with no src=, longest block wins, first max_lines meaningful lines kept.
beats.narration_text: Extract code. The actual code law. Regex over inline script tags without a source attribute — that filters out the d3 CDN import. Take the LONGEST block. That is the sim's real physics, not the boilerplate. Keep the first twenty meaningful lines. Trim any line longer than seventy-eight characters. Wrap the whole thing with a header comment naming the file, and a footer pointer to the full source.

props.title: build_cli_d3_reels.py:69-106 — extract_code()
props.code:
def extract_code(html_path, max_lines=20, max_width=78):
    """THE ACTUAL-CODE LAW: the sim's own inline JS, trimmed to what
    teaches — never pseudocode."""
    try:
        html = html_path.read_text(errors='replace')
    except OSError:
        return "// source unavailable"

    blocks = re.findall(
        r'<script(?![^>]*\bsrc=)[^>]*>(.*?)</script>',
        html, re.DOTALL | re.IGNORECASE)
    if not blocks:
        return "// no inline script found"
    js = max(blocks, key=len)                # LONGEST wins

    lines, blank_run = [], 0
    for raw in js.splitlines():
        line = raw.rstrip()
        if not line.strip():
            blank_run += 1
            if blank_run > 1 or not lines: continue
        else: blank_run = 0
        if len(line) > max_width:
            line = line[:max_width - 1] + '…'
        lines.append(line)
        if len(lines) >= max_lines: break

    return (f"// {html_path.name} — generated by Claude Code (trimmed)\n"
            f"{'\\n'.join(lines).strip()}\n"
            f"// … trimmed — full source: {html_path.name}")
props.sparkLine: Real JS. Longest block. Trim. Wrap.

beats.role_note: MECHANISM 4 — build_one() orchestrator. The 7-step subprocess dance, plus the SKIP guard on line 315.
beats.narration_text: Build one. The per sim orchestrator. Line three fifteen — if the slate mp4 is already there and over fifty kilobytes, print SKIP, append SKIP to the log, return. Otherwise: shell out to capture_sim to make output and change mp4s. Copy them to B04 and B06. Shell out to generate audio kokoro with the no gate flag. Shell out to remotion scenes for the Claude beats. Shell out to compile.py review, then to compile.py master. Every subprocess call is time boxed with a timeout in seconds.

props.title: build_cli_d3_reels.py:307-406 — build_one()
props.code:
def build_one(sim, log_file):
    reel_slug = f"claude-liam-cli-{sim['slug']}"
    reel_dir  = BOOKS_DIR / sim['book'] / "youtube" / reel_slug
    review_mp4 = reel_dir / f"{reel_slug}-slate.mp4"

    # idempotence — already-built slate short-circuits
    if review_mp4.exists() and review_mp4.stat().st_size > 50_000:
        append_log(log_file, ..., "SKIP", ..., "already built")
        return "SKIP"

    try:
        if not Path(sim['html']).exists():
            raise RuntimeError(f"HTML not found: {sim['html']}")
        (reel_dir / 'media').mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

        code = extract_code(Path(sim['html']))
        bs   = make_beat_sheet(sim, reel_slug, code)
        (reel_dir / 'beat_sheet.json').write_text(json.dumps(bs, indent=2))

        run(["python3", SCRIPTS/'capture_sim.py',   sim['html'], reel_dir],  timeout=240)
        shutil.copy(reel_dir/'media/output.mp4', reel_dir/'media/B04.mp4')
        shutil.copy(reel_dir/'media/change.mp4', reel_dir/'media/B06.mp4')
        run(["python3", SCRIPTS/'generate_audio_kokoro.py', reel_dir, '--no-gate'], timeout=600)
        run(["python3", SCRIPTS/'remotion_scenes.py',       reel_dir],             timeout=900)  # soft-fail
        run(["python3", SCRIPTS/'compile.py',               reel_dir, '--review'], timeout=600)
        run(["python3", SCRIPTS/'compile.py',               reel_dir],             timeout=600)

        append_log(log_file, ..., "BUILT", str(review_mp4), f"{size//1024}KB")
        return "BUILT"
    except Exception as e:
        append_log(log_file, ..., "FAILED", "-", str(e)[:250])
        return f"FAILED: {e}"
props.sparkLine: Seven subprocess calls. One try/except. One log row.

beats.role_note: MECHANISM 5 — falsifiability. Soft-fail on remotion_scenes (compile.py slates the missing beats). Hard-fail everywhere else logs FAILED with the message.
beats.narration_text: When things go wrong. Two failure modes. One — remotion scenes fails. The tool prints a warning to standard error and keeps going. Compile.py then slates every un rendered beat and the reel still ships as a watchable review cut. Two — anything else fails: capture, audio, compile itself. The exception is caught, the log gets a FAILED row with the message, and the loop keeps going to the next sim. Never let one bad sim take down the whole batch.

beats.role_note: VERDICT — the whole surface, one line per act.
beats.narration_text: So — build cli d3 reels dot py. The batch wrapper. One config in, N Claude skin review cuts out, one log row each. The template is fixed — ten beats, three laws, one greeting per slug. The remote dependencies are the tools it shells out to: capture sim, kokoro, remotion, compile. Every subprocess call is time boxed. Every sim can SKIP, BUILT, or FAILED. The overnight run finishes with a counts dictionary and a log file you can grep.

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW — Your Turn composer. Prompt read aloud verbatim, then discussed.
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude Code, pointed at any folder of your own D3 sims already saved as one file HTMLs. Ask Claude to write a config.json for build cli d3 reels — with one row per sim, correct slugs, books, notes — then dry run the tool. Watch whether Claude is tempted to invent notes it did not observe. That is the trap the note field exists to catch — the note becomes the beat two problem line and the title, so a fabricated note becomes a fabricated reel.

props.command: Point Claude Code at a folder that already contains N single-file D3 sim HTMLs: (1) for each .html, extract a one-line physics note by reading the file and any adjacent README; (2) draft a config.json with one sims[] row per HTML — slug from the filename, a book field, note verbatim from step 1, no title field (let make_title() run); (3) dry-run only: python3 -c 'import build_cli_d3_reels as m; ...' to call make_beat_sheet() for each row and PRINT the stamped 10 beats. Do NOT run capture_sim or compile.py yet. Do NOT invent notes you did not observe — an invented note becomes an invented reel title.
output: step 1 — one-line note per html, cited to the file/README that provided it
step 2 — config.json with N sims[] rows; no title fields; run book fields past the human
step 3 — 10 beats per sim printed as a table; the human verifies notes before capture starts
